'''Wong Siew Te'''{{Efn|{{Lang-zh|c=黄修德|p=Huáng Xiūdé}}<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-03-07 |title=黄修德：当选旅游年吉祥物 有助加强马来熊保育 |trans-title=Huang Xiude: Being Chosen as Tourism Year Mascot Helps Strengthen Sun Bear Conservation |url=https://sabah.sinchew.com.my/news/20250307/sabah/6356238 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312164038/https://sabah.sinchew.com.my/news/20250307/sabah/6356238 |archive-date=2025-03-12 |access-date=2025-08-01 |work=[[Sin Chew Daily]] |language=zh}}</ref>}} (born 16 May 1969) is a Malaysian wildlife biologist and conservationist best known for his research on the [[Malayan sun bear]].

Wong was born in 1969 in [[Bukit Mertajam]], [[Penang]], developed an early interest in animals while helping on his family's [[fruit orchard]]. He studied [[veterinary science]] in Taiwan and later [[wildlife biology]] at the [[University of Montana]], where he began focusing on sun bears. Earning a [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1997, a [[Master of Science]] in 2002, and completing doctoral research by 2011, Wong's work is driven by his goal to protect endangered sun bears and conserve [[Borneo]]'s rainforest ecosystem.

From 2002 to 2005, Wong co-chaired the [[IUCN]] Sun Bear Expert Team. In 2004, after seeing captive sun bears in poor conditions, he conceived a rescue centre, inspired by the [[Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre]]. He founded the [[Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre]] (BSBCC) in 2008, completing phase one in 2010 with 12 confiscated bears. By 2013, he continued rehabilitation efforts while collaborating with Jocelyn Stokes to raise awareness of sun bears' ecological role. In 2020, he launched virtual tours and adoption programmes to support 44 bears during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia|COVID-19 pandemic]].

== Early life and education ==
Wong Siew Te was born on 16 May 1969 in [[Bukit Mertajam]], [[Penang]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Subki |first=Sofianni |date=2023-09-28 |title=He spent half his life protecting our sun bears: Meet legendary wildlife biologist Wong Siew Te (VIDEO) |url=https://www.malaymail.com/news/life/2023/09/28/he-spent-half-his-life-protecting-our-sun-bears-meet-legendary-wildlife-biologist-wong-siew-te-video/93301 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241216132705/https://www.malaymail.com/news/life/2023/09/28/he-spent-half-his-life-protecting-our-sun-bears-meet-legendary-wildlife-biologist-wong-siew-te-video/93301 |archive-date=2024-12-16 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=[[Malay Mail]] }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-08-29 |title=Conservation Fellow: Dr. Wong Siew Te |url=https://www.sukau.com/conservation-fellow/dr-wong-siew-te/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250521073042/https://www.sukau.com/conservation-fellow/dr-wong-siew-te/ |archive-date=2025-05-21 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Sukau Rainforest Lodge }}</ref> and grew up in [[Sungai Bakap]]<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Maganathan |first=Dinesh Kumar |date=2025-07-30 |title=The man who speaks for Bornean sun bears |url=https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/leisure/2025/07/31/the-man-who-speaks-for-bornean-sun-bears |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=[[Free Malaysia Today]] }}</ref> with eight elder siblings, four brothers and four sisters.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-08-11 |title=Honourable Guest: Wong Siew Te |url=https://www.sukau.com/honourable-guest-wong-siew-te/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Sukau Rainforest Lodge }}</ref> He spent much of his childhood in the vicinity of creeks, looking after animals and helping his family cultivate their fruit orchard of [[durian]]s, [[rambutan]]s, [[mangosteen]]s, and coconuts.<ref name=":3" /> His interest in animals began early, influenced by his father, who looked after injured or fallen birds. In middle school, he learned how to breed birds and fish. He also played music and was a member of a school band.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2024-05-07 |title=馬來熊的守護者！台灣女婿黃修德肩負婆羅洲雨林的保育使命 |trans-title=Guardian of the Sun Bear! Taiwan's son-in-law Huang Xiude shoulders the mission of conserving the rainforests of [[Borneo]]. |url=https://esg.gvm.com.tw/article/58396 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250711083218/https://esg.gvm.com.tw/article/58396 |archive-date=2025-07-11 |access-date=2025-08-01 |work= |publisher=[[Central News Agency (Taiwan)|Central News Agency]] |language=zh |via=ESG遠見}}</ref> Wong attended Kin Sen Primary School from 1976 to 1981 and [[Jit Sin High School]] from 1982 to 1987, both in Bukit Mertajam.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Meet Our Crew |url=https://www.bsbcc.org.my/meet-our-crew |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre }}</ref>

Wong studied veterinary science at Taiwan's [[National Pingtung University of Science and Technology]] (NPUST) after high school in 1989, graduating in 1992.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":1" /> During his time there, he joined the Bird Watching Club, where his interest in wildlife and conservation deepened through bird watching.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Field |first=Nic |date=2022-10-20 |title=Siew Te Wong |url=https://globalanimalwelfare.org.uk/2022/10/20/siew-te-wong/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616224721/https://globalanimalwelfare.org.uk/2022/10/20/siew-te-wong/ |archive-date=2024-06-16 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Global Animal Welfare }}</ref> Wong spent two years as a research assistant in Taiwan, participating in fauna surveys, establishing a rescue centre for endangered species, and conducting radio-telemetry studies on barking deer.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Bear Necessity – A Walk on the Wild Side with Wong Siew Te |url=https://www.bsbcc.org.my/blog-february-12/a-hrefhttps10335502-143455058252546566previeweditmysitecomeditormainphp-titlelinks-active-once-publishedbear-necessity-a-walk-on-the-wild-side-with-wong-siew-tea |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250905030021/https://www.bsbcc.org.my/blog-february-12/a-hrefhttps10335502-143455058252546566previeweditmysitecomeditormainphp-titlelinks-active-once-publishedbear-necessity-a-walk-on-the-wild-side-with-wong-siew-tea |archive-date=2025-09-05 |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre}}</ref>

Wong transferred to the [[University of Montana]] in 1994 to study wildlife biology, meeting Christopher Servheen who presented him with an opportunity to study sun bears. His motive is to protect the endangered sun bear and, ultimately, to conserve the rainforest ecosystem on which both wildlife and humanity depend.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Toner |first=Kathleen |date=2017-07-27 |title=Meet the Superman saving the sun bears of Malaysia |url=https://www.cnn.com/2017/07/27/world/cnn-hero-siew-te-wong-bornean-sun-bear-conservation-centre |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231070122/https://edition.cnn.com/2017/07/27/world/cnn-hero-siew-te-wong-bornean-sun-bear-conservation-centre/ |archive-date=2019-12-31 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=[[CNN]] }}</ref> Wong graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1997 and [[Master of Science]] in 2002, authoring a thesis on Malayan sun bears in [[Borneo]]. He went on to study for a doctorate in Fish and Wildlife Biology from 2002 to 2011 at the same university, researching [[Bornean bearded pig|bearded pig]]s in lowland rainforests of Borneo.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
From 2002 to 2005, Wong co-chaired the Sun Bear Expert Team for the IUCN/SSC Bear Specialist Group, a network of voluntary experts within the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature]] (IUCN).<ref name=":1" /> In 2004, while surveying captive sun bears across Malaysia and observing their poor living conditions, he developed the idea of creating a centre to rescue and care for these neglected and little-known bears.<ref name=":2" /> Inspired by a visit to the [[Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre]], he then planned a similar facility specifically for sun bears.<ref name=":4" />

In 2007, Wong participated in filming ''BEARTREK'', a documentary set in the [[Danum Valley Conservation Area|Danum]] rainforest.<ref name=":2" /> In 2008, he founded and became CEO of the [[Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre]] (BSBCC).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tan |first=Cheng Li |date=2014-05-05 |title=Sun bears: At home in the forest |url=https://www.thestar.com.my/news/environment/2014/05/05/at-home-in-the-forest |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807191317/https://www.thestar.com.my/News/Environment/2014/05/05/At-home-in-the-forest/ |archive-date=2020-08-07 |access-date=2025-08-01 |work=[[The Star (Malaysia)|The Star]] }}</ref> The centre, located in the Sepilok–Kabili Forest Reserve, operates in partnership with the [[Sabah Wildlife Department]], the Sabah Forestry Department, and the [[NGO]] Land Empowerment Animals People to rehabilitate sun bears in a forest enclosure designed to resemble their natural habitat.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sofianni Subki |date=2023-09-28 |title=He spent half his life protecting our sun bears: Meet legendary wildlife biologist Wong Siew Te (VIDEO) |url=https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/spent-half-life-protecting-sun-022908162.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203124839/https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/spent-half-life-protecting-sun-022908162.html |archive-date=2024-12-03 |access-date=2025-08-01 |work=[[Yahoo News]] }}</ref> Wong and his team worked with the Sabah government and private funders to establish the centre in phases, beginning fundraising in November 2008. Phase one included a bear house for 20 bears and a one-hectare forest enclosure.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Neme |first=Laurel |date=2011-03-20 |title=Pet trade, palm oil, and poaching: the challenges of saving the ‘forgotten bear’ |url=https://news.mongabay.com/2011/03/pet-trade-palm-oil-and-poaching-the-challenges-of-saving-the-forgotten-bear/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250813140932/https://news.mongabay.com/2011/03/pet-trade-palm-oil-and-poaching-the-challenges-of-saving-the-forgotten-bear/ |archive-date=2025-08-13 |access-date=2025-09-05 |work=[[Mongabay|Mongabay Environmental News]] }}</ref> Malaysian actress [[Joanna Bessey]] interviewed Wong about the plight of sun bears at the BSBCC, and the program aired globally on [[BBC World News]] on 4 April 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joanna Bessey interviewed Siew Te Wong on the plights of sun bears |url=https://www.bsbcc.org.my/blog-august-09/Blog%20Post%20Title%20One-f69mw |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250905031537/https://www.bsbcc.org.my/blog-august-09/Blog%20Post%20Title%20One-f69mw |archive-date=2025-09-05 |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre}}</ref>

Phase one of the BSBCC was completed in March 2010. By May 2010, the centre housed twelve bears, all confiscated by the Sabah Wildlife Department.<ref name=":8" /> By 2013, Wong continued to lead rehabilitation efforts at the BSBCC, while Jocelyn Stokes collaborated on the ''Survival of the Sun Bears'' project, filming the bears and raising awareness of their [[ecological]] role and the threats they face from [[Deforestation in Malaysia|deforestation]] and [[poaching]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hance |first=Jeremy |date=2013-12-02 |title=New project works to raise the profile of the world’s littlest bear |url=https://news.mongabay.com/2013/12/new-project-works-to-raise-the-profile-of-the-worlds-littlest-bear/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250804010441/https://news.mongabay.com/2013/12/new-project-works-to-raise-the-profile-of-the-worlds-littlest-bear/ |archive-date=2025-08-04 |access-date=2025-09-05 |work=Mongabay Environmental News }}</ref> In May 2020, Wong launched paid virtual tours, online merchandise sales, and an adoption programme to raise awareness and funds, while continuing essential rescue operations and caring for 44 sun bears, including new cubs, despite the loss of physical visitors during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-22 |title=World's Only Sun Bear Conservation Centre Goes Virtual |url=https://sabahtourism.com/press-release/worlds-only-sun-bear-conservation-centre-goes-virtual/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240714204539/https://sabahtourism.com/press-release/worlds-only-sun-bear-conservation-centre-goes-virtual/ |archive-date=2024-07-14 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=[[Sabah Tourism Board]] }}</ref>

==Honour and recognitions==
[[File:BSBCC Sabah Wong-Siew-Te-02.jpg|thumb|Wong in 2014|230x230px]]
Wong has received numerous awards for his dedication to wildlife conservation, in particular his work with sun bears.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Awards and Recognitions |url=https://www.bsbcc.org.my/awards-and-recognitions |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre }}</ref> Among the numerous tributes is Villa Number 2 at the Sukau Rainforest Lodge, which bears his name in recognition.<ref name=":1" /> He was featured as one of the wildlife heroes in the book ''Wildlife Heroes: 40 Leading Conservationists and the Animals They Are Committed to Saving''.<ref>Julie Scardina, Jeff Flocken: [http://www.wildlifeheroes.org/ Wildlife Heroes], Running Press, 2012; {{ISBN|0762443197}}</ref> Wong received the Outstanding Alumni Award from the NPUST in 2014 for his exemplary work in wildlife conservation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-11-27 |title=103年度傑出校友－黃修德 |trans-title=Outstanding Alumnus of 2014 – Huang Xiude |url=https://news.npust.edu.tw/2014/11/27/focus-713/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=National Pingtung University of Science and Technology |language=zh-TW}}</ref>

In 2016, Wong received an Honorary Doctorate from the [[University of the Sunshine Coast]] (UniSC) in Australia for his life's work in sun bear conservation in Southeast Asia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biologist and sun bear defender receives USC Honorary Doctorate |url=https://mysunshinecoast.com.au/news/news-display/biologist-and-sun-bear-defender-receives-usc-honorary-doctorate,45920 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161008004131/https://mysunshinecoast.com.au/news/news-display/biologist-and-sun-bear-defender-receives-usc-honorary-doctorate,45920 |archive-date=2016-10-08 |access-date=2023-09-26 |website=University of the Sunshine Coast}}</ref> In 2017, he was named a {{Lang|ms|Wira Negaraku}} ({{Translation|My Country Hero|literal=yes}}) by the [[Prime Minister's Department (Malaysia)|Malaysian Prime Minister's Department]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Wong Siew Te Pengasas Pusat Konservasi Beruang Madu Borneo |trans-title=Wong Siew Te, Founder of the Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre |url=https://www.negaraku.com/cerita/wong-siew-te-pengasas-pusat-konservasi-beruang-madu-borneo/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024003307/https://www.negaraku.com/cerita/wong-siew-te-pengasas-pusat-konservasi-beruang-madu-borneo/ |archive-date=2017-10-24 |access-date=2025-08-01 |work=Negaraku |language=ms}}</ref> and later a [[CNN Heroes|CNN Hero]] by global news network CNN.<ref name=":6" /> In 2018, a genus of Asian [[stick insect]], ''[[Planososibia|Planososibia siewtei]]'', was named in his honour.<ref name=":7" /> In 2020, author Sarah Pye published ''Saving Sun Bears: One Man's Quest to Save a Species'', a biography of his conservation efforts, written as part of her creative arts doctorate at UniSC.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinclair |first=Shirley |date=2022-02-15 |title=Coast conservationist creates new hope for a little-known bear |url=https://www.sunshinecoastnews.com.au/2022/02/16/saving-sun-bears/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723035044/https://www.sunshinecoastnews.com.au/2022/02/16/saving-sun-bears/ |archive-date=2025-07-23 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Sunshine Coast News }}</ref> Wong received the President's Award from the [[International Association for Bear Research and Management]] in recognition of his 27 years of work with sun bears and 56 years in wildlife conservation.<ref>{{Cite Instagram |postid=DNt0zUT5trx |user=wongsiewte |title=It is a great honour to receive the President’s Award from the International Association for Bear Research and Management (IBA) this summer. For the past 27 years, my work with sun bears—and for 56 years with wildlife—has been driven by my passion, perseverance, and perhaps my Taurean stubbornness. My sincere thanks to IBA President John Hechtel for this significant recognition. |first=Wong |last=Siew Te |date=2025-08-24 |access-date=2025-09-05 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250905034932/https://www.instagram.com/p/DNt0zUT5trx/ |archive-date=2025-09-05 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

* [[File:MY-PEN Order of the Defender of State - Member - DJN.svg|50x50px]] Member of the [[Order of the Defender of State]] (DJN; 2014)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=The Penang Yang di-Pertuan Negeri's Birthday Honour List 2014 |url=https://sukawebnsso.penang.gov.my/pkn/Akhbar.nsf/ff4f9fa0a2840a8b482575e6002c4ea0/4681db7807786c9648257d5b002960e6/$FILE/theStar%20-%2022%20sept%202014%20-%20isu%20semasa%20pg5sm%20-%20the%20Penang%20Yg%20DiPertua.PDF |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160427023424/https://sukawebnsso.penang.gov.my/pkn/Akhbar.nsf/ff4f9fa0a2840a8b482575e6002c4ea0/4681db7807786c9648257d5b002960e6/$FILE/theStar%20-%2022%20sept%202014%20-%20isu%20semasa%20pg5sm%20-%20the%20Penang%20Yg%20DiPertua.PDF |archive-date=2016-04-27 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=The Star}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Wong is married,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-07-03 |title=Latest Conservation Fellow Dr. Wong Siew Te Visits Sukau Rainforest Lodge |url=https://www.sukau.com/latest-conservation-fellow-dr-wong-siew-te-visits-sukau-rainforest-lodge/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250808085814/https://www.sukau.com/latest-conservation-fellow-dr-wong-siew-te-visits-sukau-rainforest-lodge/ |archive-date=2025-08-08 |access-date=2025-09-05 |work=Sukau Rainforest Lodge}}</ref> and the couple has two daughters.<ref name=":2" />
